experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Safari
experiences.description: Explore the world-renowned ski slopes of Zermatt with a guided ski safari covering multiple mountain zones. Enjoy breathtaking views of the Matterhorn while carving through pristine powder on runs suitable for intermediate to advanced skiers. Includes a ski instructor for half a day to refine your technique.

experiences.name: Jungfrau Top of Europe Snow Experience
experiences.description: Take the cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters, the highest railway station in Europe. Enjoy snow tubing, a snow fun park, and stunning panoramic views of the Aletsch Glacier. A must-do alpine adventure combining sightseeing and snow activities in one unforgettable day.

experiences.name: Verbier Freeride Snowboarding
experiences.description: Experience the legendary off-piste terrain of Verbier, one of the world's top freeride destinations. Join a guided group session through untouched backcountry snow fields and steep couloirs. Safety equipment including avalanche transceiver, probe, and shovel are provided, along with a certified mountain guide.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Fondue & Raclette Evening
experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with an authentic Swiss mountain dining experience in a traditional chalet restaurant. Enjoy classic cheese fondue and raclette paired with local Swiss wines and schnapps. This cultural culinary tradition is deeply rooted in alpine heritage and offers a cozy, communal atmosphere.

experiences.name: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail
experiences.description: Glide through 100 km of groomed Nordic trails around the Davos valley, surrounded by snow-capped peaks and frozen lakes. Rent classic or skate-style cross-country skis and follow scenic routes past traditional Swiss villages. A perfect low-impact snow sport experience ideal for all fitness levels.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly SBB Swiss train from Zurich Airport to Visp (approx. 2 hrs, ~CHF 50 with a Swiss Travel Pass or half-fare card), then transfer to the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn cogwheel train to Zermatt (approx. 1.5 hrs, ~CHF 16). Check in to your Boutique Stay in Zermatt. Drop your luggage, freshen up, and take a leisurely walk through the car-free village center to get oriented. Stroll along the main Bahnhofstrasse and admire the first views of the iconic Matterhorn.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the village on foot in the early evening. Visit the small but charming Zermatt village square and browse local shops. Head back to your accommodation to rest after the long travel day.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or at the airport — grab a sandwich or pastry from a kiosk at Zurich Airport to save money (CHF 8–12).
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick bite at the Visp or Zermatt train station — a filled roll (Brötchen) or supermarket snack from Coop or Migros (CHF 6–10).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Whymper Stube in Zermatt — a cozy, budget-friendly local restaurant offering Swiss staples like rösti and cheese fondue at reasonable prices (CHF 18–25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is a car-free village — all transport within the village is by electric taxi, horse-drawn carriage, or on foot. Buy a Swiss Half-Fare Card (CHF 120) if staying more than a week — it pays off quickly. Confirm check-in time with your boutique stay in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Start your first full ski day! Head to the Zermatt Ski Area — one of the largest in the Alps. Purchase a budget day ski pass for the Rothorn/Sunnegga Paradise zone only (cheaper than the full area pass, ~CHF 60–70). Take the underground Sunnegga funicular up to 2,288m for stunning Matterhorn views and well-groomed beginner to intermediate runs. Ski the Sunnegga–Blauherd–Rothorn area all morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the Rothorn sector. Try the long Kumme run back toward Sunnegga — a classic intermediate blue/red piste with breathtaking scenery. Take a break at a mid-mountain restaurant terrace and enjoy the alpine panorama. Return your skis by 16:00 if renting to avoid late fees.
day_by_day.evening: Walk back through the village after skiing. Visit the Mountaineers' Cemetery (Bergfriedhof) — a free, poignant historical site honoring climbers who lost their lives on the Matterhorn. Wind down with hot drinks back at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique stay if included, or grab a croissant and coffee from a local bakery in the village (CHF 5–8).
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the Coop supermarket in Zermatt — sandwiches, fruit, and snacks (CHF 8–12). Eat on the mountain to save significantly vs. mountain restaurants.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries from Coop or Migros (pasta, sauce, salad) if your accommodation has a kitchen — budget CHF 10–15. Alternatively, try Pizzeria Roma in Zermatt for affordable pizza and pasta (CHF 16–22 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Ski rental tip: Rent skis from Sport Julen or Slalom Sport in the village — they offer competitive rates (~CHF 35–45/day for skis, boots, poles). Book in advance online for discounts. Avoid renting directly at the lift stations which is pricier. A helmet is strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Gornergrat Railway (book a discounted early-morning ticket online, ~CHF 44 return with half-fare card) up to 3,089m — one of the highest open-air railway stations in Europe. Arrive early to beat crowds and enjoy panoramic views of 29 four-thousand-meter peaks including the Matterhorn, Monte Rosa, and Gornergletscher glacier. Bring your camera — this is one of the most photogenic spots in Switzerland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski or snowboard down from Gornergrat through the Riffelberg area (intermediate red runs). If you prefer not to ski, take the train back down and explore the Riffelberg plateau on foot with snowshoes (rentable in the village for ~CHF 20/day). Return to the village by mid-afternoon and visit the free Matterhorn Museum (Zermatlantis) — a fascinating underground museum about the history of Zermatt and the first Matterhorn ascent (entry ~CHF 10).
day_by_day.evening: Relax in the village. Browse the free-to-enter local art galleries or simply enjoy the magical twilight views of the illuminated Matterhorn from the village. Try a self-guided evening walk along the Vispa river path.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before catching the Gornergrat train — instant oats or bread with spreads prepared in your room, or a bakery stop (CHF 5–8).
meals.lunch: Bring a packed lunch from Coop to eat at the Gornergrat summit — the views are free, the sandwiches should be too (CHF 8–12). Hot thermos of tea or coffee recommended at altitude.
meals.dinner: Try Restaurant Weisshorn in Zermatt for traditional Swiss dishes — look for the daily set menu (Tagesmenü) which typically offers soup + main for CHF 18–24.

day_by_day.notes: The Gornergrat Railway is not included in the ski pass — it's a separate ticket. Book online in advance for a 10–15% discount. Dress in warm layers — temperatures at 3,089m can be significantly colder than the village. Sunscreen is essential at high altitude even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Saas-Fee — a neighboring car-free Alpine village with excellent skiing and a more budget-friendly ski pass (~CHF 50–60/day). Take the PostBus from Zermatt to Visp, then another bus to Saas-Fee (approx. 1.5–2 hrs total, ~CHF 15 each way with half-fare card). Saas-Fee sits at 1,800m and offers glacier skiing up to 3,600m. Ski the Metro Alpin area — Europe's highest underground funicular leads to stunning glacier runs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing in Saas-Fee. Try the Felskinn–Mittelallalin area with wide, well-groomed pistes. Visit the Ice Pavilion (Eispavilion) inside the glacier — a unique ice cave with sculptures carved into the glacial ice (included in some ski passes or ~CHF 5 separately). Begin heading back to Zermatt by 15:30 to catch comfortable return buses.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zermatt by early evening. Rest your legs and enjoy a quiet evening. Take a short night walk to the famous Matterhorn viewpoint near the Gornergrat railway station for dramatic after-dark mountain silhouette views.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast in your room before the early departure (bread, cheese, fruit bought from Coop the day before — CHF 5).
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from Coop to take to Saas-Fee — saves significantly compared to mountain restaurants (CHF 8–12). Alternatively, Saas-Fee village has a Migros supermarket for affordable hot food.
meals.dinner: Back in Zermatt — try the Café du Pont for affordable Swiss-style comfort food and warm soups (CHF 15–22 per person). Great après-ski atmosphere without the steep prices.

day_by_day.notes: Check PostBus schedules in advance at sbb.ch — buses between Zermatt area and Saas-Fee are not frequent. Confirm the last bus return time before you go. Saas-Fee ski passes can be purchased online for small discounts. This is a full day so start early — aim to leave Zermatt by 08:00.

day_by_day.morning: Free skiing day in the Zermatt ski area — focus on the Klein Matterhorn (Matterhorn Glacier Paradise) sector, the highest cable car station in the Alps at 3,883m. Purchase a half-day afternoon pass or use a full-day pass (~CHF 75 full area). Take the cable car up to the Klein Matterhorn and ski the legendary glacier runs. On clear days, views extend to Mont Blanc in France and peaks in Italy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski the Italian side — take the Theodul Pass runs down toward Cervinia, Italy (check border crossing is open and included in your pass — the international Zermatt–Cervinia pass costs more but is a once-in-a-trip experience). Alternatively, ski back to Zermatt via the Furggsattel and Schwarzsee area. By 15:00, try snowshoeing near the Schwarzsee lake area — a beautiful, peaceful alternative to the busy pistes (snowshoe rental ~CHF 20).
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a budget-friendly fondue night — fondue is actually very affordable when shared. Head to Restaurant du Pont or a local fondue spot and share a classic cheese fondue between two people (CHF 20–28 per person). This is a quintessential Swiss Alps experience.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast to fuel a big ski day — boiled eggs, bread, and yogurt from supermarket supplies in your room (CHF 5–7), or a café breakfast (CHF 10–14).
meals.lunch: On the mountain — pack snacks (energy bars, nuts, fruit) and a thermos to minimize costs. If you want a hot meal, look for the more affordable self-service mountain huts rather than sit-down restaurants (CHF 12–18 for a hot dish).
meals.dinner: Fondue dinner at a local restaurant — a memorable and surprisingly budget-friendly Swiss experience when shared. Budget CHF 22–30 per person including a drink.

day_by_day.notes: The Klein Matterhorn cable car can have long queues on weekends — arrive at the base station early (before 09:00). The glacier area at 3,883m requires warm, windproof clothing even on sunny days — temperatures can drop to -15°C or lower with wind chill. Altitude sickness is rare but possible — stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Rest your legs from skiing! Take a free winter hiking trail from the village — the path along the Vispa river toward Täsch is flat, scenic, and completely free. Alternatively, walk up to the Winkelmatten chapel for beautiful elevated village views. Spend the morning exploring the quieter back streets of Zermatt, visiting the free-entry Protestant church and admiring traditional Walliser wooden chalets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the free Sunnegga shuttle (or walk up the trail) and try cross-country skiing or snowshoeing on the Sunnegga plateau — a much cheaper alternative to downhill skiing (snowshoe rental ~CHF 20, trails are free). The views of the Matterhorn from Sunnegga are among the best anywhere. Return to the village by 16:00 and visit the Zermatt Alpine Museum (small entry fee ~CHF 5) for local history and mountaineering exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Saturday evening in Zermatt has a lively atmosphere — enjoy a budget-friendly drink at one of the village bars (happy hour deals available). Try the Papperla Pub for a relaxed après-ski vibe with reasonably priced drinks. Walk the illuminated village at night for a magical final full weekend evening.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a sit-down breakfast at a local café — try Café Biner or a village bakery for fresh bread, jam, and coffee (CHF 10–15).
meals.lunch: Supermarket lunch from Coop or Migros — pick up a warm soup cup, bread roll, and fruit (CHF 8–12). Eat outside if the weather allows — the mountain views make any meal special.
meals.dinner: Cook a final budget dinner in your accommodation if possible — pasta with local Swiss cheese melted in (a nod to fondue) using supermarket ingredients (CHF 12–15 for two). Or try Zermatt's affordable kebab/döner shop near the train station for a quick CHF 10–14 meal.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day in Zermatt as new weekly guests arrive — ski lifts and restaurants will be more crowded. This is a great day to take a break from skiing and explore the village and surroundings on foot. Check if your boutique stay has any late checkout options for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Zermatt — wake up early for one last sunrise view of the Matterhorn from the village. Take a slow walk to the Matterhorn viewpoint near the Gornergrat railway station or the bridge over the Vispa river for iconic photos. Pack your bags and check out of your boutique stay (store luggage at reception if needed).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your last few hours doing a final village stroll and picking up affordable Swiss souvenirs — look for local cheese (Raclette or Gruyère from the Coop), Swiss chocolate (Lindt or Cailler bars from the supermarket are much cheaper than tourist shops), or a simple Matterhorn postcard. Head to Zermatt train station and take the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn back to Visp, then connect to your onward train to Zurich or your departure airport. Enjoy the scenic valley views on the way out.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or onward travel. If your flight is the next day, consider an affordable overnight stay near Zurich Airport (budget hotels from CHF 80–100) rather than an expensive last-minute city hotel. Enjoy a final Swiss meal at a train station restaurant — SBB station restaurants offer reasonable daily menus (CHF 16–22).

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast in Zermatt — use up any remaining supermarket supplies (bread, cheese, fruit) to minimize waste and cost (CHF 5). Or splurge slightly on a farewell café breakfast (CHF 12–16).
meals.lunch: Pack a travel lunch from Coop for the train journey — sandwiches, snacks, and a drink (CHF 8–12). Train dining cars are expensive — avoid them.
meals.dinner: At Zurich train station (Zürich HB) — the station has a wide range of affordable options including Coop to go, Tibits (vegetarian buffet by weight, ~CHF 14–18), or a Migros restaurant for hot meals (CHF 12–16).

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your train connections at sbb.ch the night before — Sunday afternoon trains from Zermatt can be busy with departing guests. Book seats in advance if possible. Declare any food items (especially meat/dairy) when crossing back into EU if applicable. Keep all ski rental return receipts and check your deposit has been refunded.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to Zermatt via train (Zurich/Geneva → Visp → Zermatt, approx. 3–3.5 hours). Note: Zermatt is car-free, so transfer luggage via electric taxi or porter service at Täsch terminal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Boutique Stay in Zermatt (~16:30). Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed orientation walk through the charming car-free village. Visit the base of the Matterhorn viewpoint near the church for iconic first views. Pick up your ski passes and rent equipment from a local shop (e.g., Slalom Sport or Bayard Sport) to be ready for Day 2.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Zermatt's Bahnhofstrasse for a gentle introduction to the village atmosphere. Enjoy a welcome dinner at a cozy local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: In-flight meal or grab a snack at the airport/train station (Zürich HB has great bakeries like Sprüngli)
meals.lunch: Quick bite at Visp or Täsch train station — pick up a Swiss sandwich (Sandwich mit Käse) or a warm pretzel from a station kiosk (~CHF 8–12)
meals.dinner: Whymper Stube (Zermatt) — a classic mid-range mountain restaurant offering Swiss staples like Rösti, Älplermagronen, and local sausages. Budget ~CHF 30–45 per person including a beer or wine.

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is accessible only by train — no private cars allowed beyond Täsch. Book a luggage porter in advance if your boutique stay is not near the station. Exchange currency or use card; CHF is standard. Check ski rental reservation online to save time.

day_by_day.morning: Zermatt Ski Safari (Part 1) — Join the guided Zermatt Ski Safari starting at 09:00 from the Klein Matterhorn (Matterhorn Glacier Paradise) cable car. Your guide will lead you across Zermatt's 360 km of groomed pistes spanning three valleys. Morning focus: the high-altitude glacier runs above 3,800 m with breathtaking Matterhorn views. Intermediate to advanced terrain recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Ski Safari into the afternoon covering the Rothorn and Sunnegga Paradise sectors. The guide will tailor routes based on group ability. Take a mid-mountain lunch break with panoramic views before continuing to the lower Findeln area runs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to village by 16:30. Relax at your boutique hotel — many offer a wellness area or sauna, perfect for tired muscles. Head out for a leisurely evening stroll along the illuminated village streets.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a local café — try Café du Pont for fresh croissants, birchermüesli, and coffee (~CHF 12–18)
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch included or recommended with the ski safari — Chez Vrony on the Findeln slope is a beloved mid-range spot with stunning Matterhorn views. Rösti with fried egg and local cheese (~CHF 25–35)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Stockhorn Grill, Zermatt — hearty après-ski dining with Swiss-Italian influences. Try the fondue or grilled meats. ~CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Zermatt Ski Safari in advance as guided spots fill quickly in February. Wear layered clothing — temperatures at 3,800 m can be -15°C or colder even on sunny days. Sunscreen and glacier goggles are essential. Ski Safari typically lasts 6–7 hours including breaks.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfrau Top of Europe Snow Experience — Depart Zermatt early by 07:30 train to Interlaken (via Visp, ~2.5 hours), then connect to the Jungfraujoch cogwheel railway from Grindelwald or Lauterbrunnen. Arrive at Jungfraujoch (3,454 m) by ~11:00. Explore the Ice Palace, Sphinx Observatory, and walk on the Aletsch Glacier plateau — the longest glacier in the Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Jungfraujoch — enjoy the Snow Fun Park (sledding, snow tubing, zip line on the glacier). Take the cogwheel train back down to Kleine Scheidegg for a scenic stop, then return to Interlaken by ~15:30. Begin return journey toward Zermatt, arriving ~18:30.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening back in Zermatt. Visit the Matterhorn Museum (Zermatlantis) for a fascinating look at alpine history and the first ascent of the Matterhorn (~CHF 10 entry). Then dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before 07:30 departure — pack an energy bar or grab a pastry at Zermatt station
meals.lunch: Self-Service Restaurant at Jungfraujoch Top of Europe — panoramic views with Swiss classics like goulash soup, sandwiches, and hot chocolate. Budget ~CHF 20–30
meals.dinner: Restaurant Papperla Pub, Zermatt — lively, affordable après-ski atmosphere with burgers, pasta, and Swiss dishes. ~CHF 25–38 per person. Great for a relaxed mid-week evening.

day_by_day.notes: Jungfraujoch is a full-day excursion from Zermatt — an early start is essential. Purchase Jungfrau Railway tickets in advance online (Swiss Travel Pass may offer discounts). Altitude sickness is possible at 3,454 m — ascend slowly, stay hydrated, and avoid alcohol until back at lower altitude. Dress in full winter gear; temperatures are extreme at the summit.

day_by_day.morning: Free skiing day in Zermatt — explore the Sunnegga–Rothorn sector independently. Take the underground funicular to Sunnegga (2,288 m) and ride up to Rothorn (3,103 m). Enjoy wide, well-groomed blue and red runs perfect for a relaxed mid-trip ski day. Stop at the Fluhalp mountain hut for a mid-morning coffee with Matterhorn views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Verbier Freeride Snowboarding Experience — Arrange a half-day transfer or join an organized group excursion to Verbier (approx. 1.5 hours from Zermatt by car/shuttle). Work with a certified freeride guide to explore Verbier's legendary off-piste terrain including the Vallon d'Arby and Mont-Fort sectors. Suitable for confident intermediate to advanced riders and skiers.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zermatt by early evening (~18:30). Unwind with a wellness session (sauna or hot tub) at your boutique hotel or a local spa. Enjoy a special Swiss Alpine Fondue & Raclette Evening — the highlight cultural dining experience of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up well before a full day of skiing and travel
meals.lunch: Grab a quick mountain lunch in Verbier at Le Fer à Cheval — a classic Verbier brasserie with raclette sandwiches and hearty soups (~CHF 20–28)
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue & Raclette Evening experience in Zermatt — book a traditional chalet restaurant such as Restaurant Schäferstube or Le Mazot. Authentic cheese fondue, raclette, and charcuterie with local Valais wine. ~CHF 45–60 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Verbier freeride experience requires booking a private or group guide — contact a Verbier ski school (e.g., Ski School Verbier Evolution 2) in advance. Off-piste terrain carries avalanche risk; ensure your guide provides or rents avalanche safety equipment (beacon, probe, shovel). Confirm shuttle or transfer logistics the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail — Depart Zermatt by 07:45 train toward Davos (via Visp → Chur → Davos, ~3.5 hours). Arrive ~11:15. Begin your Nordic skiing experience on the 100 km of groomed trails around the Davos valley. Start with the scenic Flüelastrasse trail — a gentle classic-style track with stunning snow-capped mountain panoramas ideal for all fitness levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Nordic skiing on the Davos-Klosters trail network. Try the skate-skiing technique on the wider sections with guidance from a local instructor if desired (book at the Davos Nordic Center). Explore the lakeside trails around Davosersee for a picturesque afternoon loop (~10–15 km total for the day).
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Zermatt (arriving ~20:00 — a long but rewarding day). Enjoy a lighter, relaxed dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or a bakery stop at Zermatt station before departure
meals.lunch: Café Schneider, Davos Platz — a beloved local bakery and café with homemade soups, sandwiches, and Swiss pastries. ~CHF 15–22
meals.dinner: Grampi's Pub & Restaurant, Zermatt — casual, mid-range dining with pasta, salads, and Swiss classics. Perfect for a relaxed late dinner after a long travel day. ~CHF 28–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Davos day trip is long due to travel time (~7 hours total transit). Consider whether to shorten the itinerary or spend a night in Davos if preferred — however, returning to Zermatt keeps accommodation costs consistent. Nordic ski rental is available at Davos Nordic Center (CHF 25–35/day). A Swiss Travel Pass covers most train segments — verify validity in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed free morning in Zermatt — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Take a scenic snowshoe hike on the marked trails around Zermatt (e.g., Zermatt–Furi–Schwarzsee trail). Snowshoe rental available at most sport shops (~CHF 20–25/day). The Schwarzsee area offers spectacular close-up views of the Matterhorn's north face.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the slopes for a final afternoon ski session — revisit your favorite runs or explore the Italian side of the Klein Matterhorn (Cervinia, Italy) if your ski pass covers it. The Matterhorn Glacier Paradise cable car to 3,883 m offers Europe's highest ski terrain. Enjoy the surreal experience of skiing between Switzerland and Italy.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory final full evening in Zermatt. Explore the village boutiques for Swiss souvenirs (chocolate, cheese, watches). Enjoy a special farewell dinner at one of Zermatt's finest mid-range restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent hotel breakfast — take your time and enjoy the full spread
meals.lunch: Riffelhaus 1853 restaurant (reachable by Gornergrat railway) — panoramic terrace lunch with Matterhorn and Monte Rosa views. Rösti, mountain soup, and local beer. ~CHF 30–42
meals.dinner: Restaurant du Pont, Zermatt — elegant yet approachable fine dining with Swiss-French cuisine. Try the veal with morel mushrooms or the Valais lamb. ~CHF 50–70 per person with wine — a worthy splurge for the final evening.

day_by_day.notes: Check ski pass terms for Italy (Cervinia) access — a cross-border extension may require an upgrade (~CHF 20–30 extra). Saturday is typically the busiest day on Zermatt slopes; start early to beat lift queues. Begin packing in the evening and confirm departure logistics for Day 7.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Zermatt — check out of boutique hotel (standard checkout 11:00). Store luggage with the hotel concierge. Take one last walk to the Matterhorn viewpoint near the English Church for a final photo. Browse the village market (if running on Sundays) for last-minute Swiss chocolates (Läderach or local brands) and regional Valais wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Zermatt by train toward your departure airport (Zurich ~3.5 hrs, Geneva ~3 hrs via Visp). Enjoy the scenic Rhône Valley train journey as a final alpine farewell. Arrive at airport with ample time for check-in and departure formalities.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on an incredible week of world-class skiing, stunning alpine scenery, Swiss culture, and mountain gastronomy.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy a full Swiss breakfast with local cheeses, cold cuts, birchermüesli, and fresh bread
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Zermatt station or on the train — pick up a sandwich and Swiss chocolate at the station kiosk (~CHF 10–15)
meals.dinner: Airport dining at departure terminal, or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm train times from Zermatt to your departure airport the evening before — Sunday schedules may vary slightly. Allow extra time at Täsch to transfer luggage to the train. Duty-free shopping at Swiss airports is excellent for last-minute chocolate and watches. Ensure ski rental equipment is returned by Day 6 evening or early Day 7 morning to avoid extra charges.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with an authentic Swiss mountain dining experience in a traditional chalet restaurant. Enjoy classic cheese fondue and raclette paired with local Swiss wines and schnapps. This cultural culinary tradition is deeply rooted in alpine heritage and offers a cozy, communal atmosphere.

experiences.name: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail
experiences.description: Glide through 100 km of groomed Nordic trails around the Davos valley, surrounded by snow-capped peaks and frozen lakes. Rent classic or skate-style cross-country skis and follow scenic routes past traditional Swiss villages. A perfect low-impact snow sport experience ideal for all fitness levels.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Transfer from airport to Zermatt via private luxury rail or helicopter transfer arranged by the boutique hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private welcome orientation at the boutique stay in Zermatt, Valais. Check-in, champagne welcome, and a personal concierge briefing on the week's schedule. Take a leisurely stroll along the car-free Bahnhofstrasse to acclimatize to the altitude and soak in the first iconic views of the Matterhorn.
day_by_day.evening: Settle in with a refined dinner at a top Zermatt restaurant. Enjoy the ambiance and begin your alpine luxury experience with a curated Swiss wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge dining)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (arriving at 13:00 — light snack provided during private transfer)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Chez Vrony on the Findeln alp — one of Zermatt's most celebrated mountain restaurants. Savor regional dishes like Valais lamb and seasonal alpine vegetables, paired with premier Swiss Fendant white wine, with sweeping Matterhorn views illuminated in the evening light.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private helicopter or luxury Glacier Express transfer in advance. Zermatt is a car-free village — hotel electric taxi will meet you at Täsch parking station. Hydrate well on arrival to ease altitude acclimatization at 1,608 m.

day_by_day.morning: Zermatt Ski Safari — Day 1: Begin your guided ski safari on the legendary Zermatt slopes. A certified private mountain guide leads you across the Klein Matterhorn sector (3,883 m), tackling groomed red and black runs with breathtaking panoramic views of 38 four-thousand-meter peaks. Start with warm-up runs on the Rothorn plateau.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Zermatt Ski Safari across the Sunnegga-Rothorn and Gornergrat sectors. Cover multiple mountain zones linked by Zermatt's 360 km of pistes. Pause for a gourmet mountain lunch mid-slope before exploring the Italian border runs accessible via the Matterhorn glacier paradise.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique hotel for a private in-room spa treatment (hot stone massage or après-ski deep tissue treatment) arranged by the concierge. Followed by the Swiss Alpine Fondue & Raclette Evening experience — gather in a traditional chalet-style restaurant for an authentic mountain dining ceremony with artisanal Gruyère and Appenzeller fondue, accompanied by local charcuterie and crisp Chasselas wine.

meals.breakfast: Sumptuous buffet breakfast at the boutique hotel — fresh Swiss pastries, local cheeses, charcuterie, bircher muesli, eggs prepared to order, and freshly squeezed juices.
meals.lunch: Gourmet on-mountain lunch at Findlerhof or Olympia Stübli — enjoy truffle risotto, venison carpaccio, or hearty alpine soup with artisan bread, served slope-side.
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue & Raclette Evening at a traditional Zermatt chalet restaurant such as Walliserkanne — bubbling cheese fondue, raclette, air-dried Valais beef (Bündnerfleisch), and a curated Swiss wine flight.

day_by_day.notes: Ensure ski equipment is fitted the evening before at a premium ski rental boutique (e.g., Slalom Sport or Bayard Sport). A private guide is strongly recommended for the ski safari — book through the hotel concierge. Dress in high-performance layered ski wear; temperatures at altitude can reach -15°C.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfrau Top of Europe Snow Experience — Depart Zermatt by private car to Grindelwald or Lauterbrunnen (approx. 2.5-hour scenic drive or arrange a private helicopter transfer for a dramatic alpine arrival). Board the iconic cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 m — the highest railway station in Europe. Marvel at the Aletsch Glacier, the longest glacier in the Alps, and enjoy the Sphinx Observatory viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ice Palace carved deep within the glacier, walk the Plateau Trail snowshoeing path, and experience the Snow Fun Park with sledges and zip lines. Enjoy exclusive access to the Top of Europe panoramic terrace. Return by cogwheel train in the late afternoon with a stop in Kleine Scheidegg for views of the Eiger North Face.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zermatt via private transfer. Wind down at the hotel's private lounge or spa. Enjoy a sophisticated dinner at one of Zermatt's Michelin-starred or top-tier fine dining establishments.

meals.breakfast: Early in-hotel breakfast before departure — continental spread with Swiss mountain honey, local jams, warm croissants, and espresso.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Crystal Restaurant at Jungfraujoch (Top of Europe) — a unique dining experience at 3,454 m with panoramic glacier views. Enjoy a warm alpine menu including Swiss rösti, mountain soups, and hot drinks.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Restaurant Zum See in Zermatt — a legendary intimate mountain restaurant renowned for its creative European alpine cuisine, exceptional wine cellar, and candlelit chalet atmosphere. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Jungfraujoch requires advance ticket booking — the hotel concierge should arrange VIP or priority access passes. Altitude at Jungfraujoch (3,454 m) is significantly higher than Zermatt; bring sunscreen SPF 50+, UV glacier goggles, and warm layers. A private helicopter transfer between Zermatt and Jungfrau region is available and highly recommended for the full luxury experience.

day_by_day.morning: Verbier Freeride Snowboarding Experience — Depart Zermatt early for Verbier (approx. 1.5-hour private transfer). Meet your certified IFMGA mountain guide for an introduction to Verbier's legendary off-piste terrain. Begin with a safety briefing, avalanche transceiver fitting, and a warm-up run on the Mont-Fort glacier (3,330 m). Tackle iconic freeride lines on the Stairway to Heaven and Tortin couloir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue freeride exploration across Verbier's vast off-piste terrain — powder fields, steep couloirs, and hidden backcountry routes only accessible with a professional guide. Experience why Verbier hosts the Xtreme Freeride World Tour. Option for a heli-skiing drop in an exclusive untracked powder zone (weather permitting — premium add-on).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zermatt by private transfer. Enjoy a well-deserved relaxation session at the hotel spa or private jacuzzi. Dinner at a cozy Zermatt restaurant with a focus on Valais regional cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — high-energy options including granola, protein-rich eggs, smoked salmon, and freshly brewed Swiss mountain herbal tea.
meals.lunch: Lunch at La Vache in Verbier — a legendary après-ski and mountain dining institution known for its premium Angus burgers, seafood platters, and festive alpine atmosphere. Perfectly located slope-side.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Schäferstube at Hotel Monte Rosa in Zermatt — a refined Swiss-French alpine menu featuring seasonal game, truffle dishes, and an extensive cellar of Rhône Valley and Burgundy wines.

day_by_day.notes: Verbier freeride terrain is for advanced to expert skiers and snowboarders only. A certified guide with avalanche equipment (transceiver, probe, shovel) is mandatory — non-negotiable for safety. Heli-skiing in Verbier requires advance booking and is subject to Swiss aviation and weather regulations. Confirm fitness level and experience honestly with your guide.

day_by_day.morning: Zermatt Ski Safari — Day 2: Return to Zermatt's slopes for a second guided ski safari, this time focusing on the Gornergrat sector. Ride the historic Gornergrat Cog Railway to 3,089 m for a different perspective of the Matterhorn and Monte Rosa massif. Ski down long, sweeping runs through the Riffelalp and Riffelberg zones — ideal for high-speed carving on pristine groomed pistes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the cross-border skiing experience — ski from Zermatt into Cervinia, Italy via the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise. Enjoy a true international alpine adventure covering two countries in one afternoon. Ski back across the border before the last lifts close. Optional private snowmobile excursion on a designated route for an adrenaline-fueled afternoon add-on.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a full luxury spa evening at the hotel — private sauna, steam room, and a 90-minute couples or solo alpine herbal wrap treatment. Followed by a private in-suite dining experience with a curated tasting menu prepared by a private chef arranged by the hotel concierge.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss hotel breakfast — warm porridge with alpine berry compote, eggs Benedict, smoked trout, artisan cheeses, and fresh fruit platters.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Cervinia, Italy — dine at a traditional Italian mountain trattoria slope-side. Enjoy handmade pasta, osso buco, and a glass of Barolo before skiing back to Switzerland.
meals.dinner: Private in-suite gourmet dining experience — a 5-course tasting menu curated by the hotel's private chef, featuring Valais lamb, black truffle, alpine herbs, and a paired wine flight of Swiss Grand Cru and Burgundy selections. White-glove table service in your suite.

day_by_day.notes: Cross-border skiing to Cervinia requires a valid passport or EU ID — carry identification on the slopes. The Matterhorn Glacier Paradise lift connecting Zermatt and Cervinia is the highest cable car in the Alps (3,883 m). Check lift operating hours as Italy-side lifts may close earlier. The private chef dinner must be arranged 48 hours in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail Experience — Depart Zermatt by private car or train to Davos (approx. 3-hour scenic journey through the Swiss Alps). Arrive in Davos and begin gliding through 100 km of immaculately groomed Nordic trails across the Davos valley. A private Nordic skiing instructor accompanies you through the classic and skate-skiing trails, surrounded by snow-capped peaks and pristine winter forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Nordic exploration along the Flüela Valley trail — one of the most scenic cross-country routes in Switzerland. Pause for a lakeside rest at Davosersee, frozen and blanketed in snow. Optional winter wellness walk or snowshoeing detour through the Sertig Valley for those preferring a gentler pace. Return to Davos town center for a warm-up.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zermatt by private transfer. Enjoy a final evening of pure luxury — reserve a table at Zermatt's finest restaurant for a celebratory dinner marking the penultimate night of your alpine journey.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure — light and energizing: Swiss muesli, yogurt with alpine honey, whole grain bread, and green tea.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bergrestaurant Schatzalp in Davos — a stunning Art Nouveau mountain hotel restaurant accessible only by funicular, offering panoramic valley views and a refined Swiss mountain menu including venison ragout, alpine cheese boards, and warm Glühwein.
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Restaurant Capri at The Omnia Hotel in Zermatt — an exclusive cliff-top restaurant with floor-to-ceiling windows framing the Matterhorn. Enjoy a refined Mediterranean-Alpine fusion menu with premium seafood, wagyu beef, and an award-winning wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Davos is a full-day excursion from Zermatt — an early departure (7:30–8:00 AM) is recommended to maximize time on the Nordic trails. Davos sits at 1,560 m and has a different microclimate from Zermatt — pack an extra wind-resistant layer. Nordic ski equipment can be rented in Davos at premium sport shops near the train station.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Zermatt — a leisurely sunrise snowshoe walk to the Riffelalp viewpoint for a last, unhurried communion with the Matterhorn at golden hour. Return for a long, indulgent farewell breakfast at the hotel. Browse Zermatt's boutique shops along Bahnhofstrasse for premium Swiss souvenirs — fine Swiss watches, artisan chocolates, and local Valais wines to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the boutique hotel. Private luxury transfer from Zermatt to Zürich Airport or Geneva Airport depending on departure flight. En route, optional stop at a renowned Swiss chocolate atelier (e.g., Läderach or Sprüngli in Zürich) for a final Swiss indulgence before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland. Relax in a premium airport lounge with a final glass of Swiss Chasselas or single-malt Scotch, reflecting on an extraordinary week in the Swiss Alps.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the boutique hotel — the full spread: eggs any style, smoked salmon, artisan Swiss cheeses, warm pastries, fresh fruit, freshly squeezed juices, and barista-prepared coffee and teas. Unhurried and indulgent.
meals.lunch: Light gourmet lunch en route to the airport — a curated picnic hamper prepared by the hotel featuring artisan sandwiches, local charcuterie, Swiss chocolates, and sparkling mineral water, enjoyed during the private transfer through the alpine landscape.
meals.dinner: Airport fine dining or premium airline lounge dining — alternatively, if time permits before departure, dinner at Clouds Restaurant atop Prime Tower in Zürich for a panoramic urban farewell to Switzerland.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–3.5 hours for the Zermatt-to-Zürich Airport transfer and check-in for international flights. The hotel concierge should arrange luggage forwarding or porter service. Consider purchasing a selection of local Valais wines, Läderach Grand Cru chocolates, and Swiss specialty foods as premium gifts. Confirm all private transfer bookings 24 hours before departure.
